short_definition: argument_compares_to_scientific_or_historical_norms: OP argument: 1 if the OP's own argument explicitly compares its claim, case or proposal to an established scientific or historical norm; else 0.

op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation: OP title and argument, OP's own voice: 1 if the OP explicitly expresses fear of social rejection or isolation (e.g., being rejected, ostracized, judged out, or left alone by others).

op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense: OP title and argument, OP's own voice: 1 if the OP states beliefs with no emotional self-defense (no expressed fear, hurt, defensiveness or self-protective emotional appeal about themselves).

fear_rejection_vs_no_self_defense_group: OP title and argument: 1 if the OP expresses explicit fear of social rejection or isolation, 0 if the OP states beliefs without emotional self-defense, null otherwise.

any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent: Other-user comments: 1 if at least one comment cites a specific, functioning institutional precedent (an actual existing institution, law, policy or system that operates in practice) as support for its counter-argument.

any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles: Other-user comments: 1 if at least one comment relies on abstract normative principles (e.g. fairness, rights, morality, justice) as its argument basis.
supplied_log_length: Supplied log_length column: the precomputed log-transformed length value for the discussion row, used as given.
op_argument_admits_uncertainty: OP argument: 1 if the OP explicitly admits their own uncertainty or possible error about their view or claims.
op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty: OP argument: 1 if the OP explicitly asserts absolute certainty in their own view (no room for being wrong).

distinct_op_factual_premises_challenged: OC_comments (other users' comments) read against the OP argument: count of distinct factual premises stated in the OP argument that are challenged by at least one comment.
oc_comment_count: OC_comments: number of counter-argument comments by other users in the parsed list
distinct_counterargument_count: OC_comments (other users' comments): number of semantically distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view, deduplicated across comments
has_at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments: OC_comments: 1 if `distinct_counterargument_count` >= 3, else 0
title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers: OP title: 1 if the title uses absolute certainty markers (e.g., wording asserting the claim as certain, universal or beyond doubt, without hedging); else 0
op_invites_critique_or_tentative: OP title and argument (OP's own voice): 1 if the OP explicitly invites critique/challenge or uses tentative/hedged language about their own view, else 0.
op_uses_absolute_definitive_declarations: OP title and argument (OP's own voice): 1 if the OP states their view in absolute, definitive declarations, else 0.

any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example: OC_comments (other users' counter-argument comments): 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example (actual case, event, person, institution, or concrete personal experience, not invented/hypothetical) in support of its argument.
share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning: OC_comments (other users' comments): share of comments containing measured, logical reasoning (calm, structured inference from premises to conclusion)
share_comments_emotional_aggression: OC_comments (other users' comments): share of comments containing emotional aggression (hostile, angry, insulting or belligerent affect toward the OP or others)
logical_minus_aggressive_comment_share: OC_comments: share of comments with measured logical reasoning minus share with emotional aggression

any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim: OC_comments (other users): 1 if at least one comment, within the same comment, explicitly quotes specific OP wording and refutes that same OP factual claim; endorsement not required.

any_comment_validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction: Other-user comments: at least one single comment explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity or effort and then, later in that same comment, introduces corrective logic
all_comments_purely_logical_refutation: Other-user comments: every comment is a purely logical refutation with no explicit validation of the OP's personal dignity or effort

any_comment_concrete_real_world_example: Other-user counter-argument comments: 1 if at least one comment provides a concrete real-world example (specific actual case, including a specific personal experience); invented/hypothetical scenarios do not count.

any_comment_engages_op_cited_examples_or_premises: Other-user comments: at least one comment explicitly engages (addresses, rebuts, or builds on) a specific example or premise cited in the OP's title/argument text.

any_comment_concrete_personal_labor_details: Other-user comments: at least one comment introduces concrete, personal labor-process details (specific first-hand work tasks, workplace procedures or job experiences of the commenter or someone concretely described).
all_comments_solely_abstract_normative: Other-user comments: every comment relies solely on abstract normative principles, with no concrete personal details.

any_comment_quantifies_systemic_material_harm_to_third_parties: Other-user comments: at least one comment explicitly quantifies systemic material harm to third parties (people other than the commenter/OP debate participants), using numbers, rates, amounts or magnitudes.
any_comment_asserts_propositional_falsity: Other-user comments: at least one comment asserts that an OP proposition or claim is factually or logically false/incorrect.

any_comment_identifies_op_internal_contradiction: Other-user comments: 1 if at least one comment identifies a logical contradiction or inconsistency within the OP's own stated premises (title/argument).

any_comment_cites_external_evidence: Other-user comments: 1 if at least one comment cites external evidence (e.g. data, studies, sources, or documented real-world facts/cases) in support of its counter-argument.
any_comment_specific_factual_data_or_citation: OC_comments (other users' counter-argument comments): 1 if at least one comment provides specific factual data or a verifiable citation
argument_has_polite_apology_phrase: OP argument: 1 if it contains at least one explicit polite apology phrase by the OP (e.g., sorry, I apologize, apologies, pardon me, excuse me); else 0.

op_first_person_vulnerable_admission: OP's own title/argument text: 1 if the OP makes at least one first-person vulnerable admission (OP discloses in their own voice a personal weakness, fear, failure, insecurity, mistake or emotionally exposing experience).

op_third_person_distant_observation: OP's own title/argument text: 1 if the OP presents at least one distant, third-person observation (detached description of other people, groups, institutions or events, not about the OP's own experience).

vulnerable_admission_vs_distant_observation_only: OP title/argument: 1 if first-person vulnerable admission is present and distant third-person observation absent; 0 if the reverse; null if both or neither present.
any_comment_contains_url: OC_comments: 1 if at least one other-user comment contains a literal direct URL or external hyperlink; else 0.

any_comment_specific_verifiable_procedural_example: Other-user comments: at least one comment employs a specific, verifiable procedural example (a concrete named or checkable process, rule, procedure or documented case of how something is done) in its counter-argument.
all_comments_solely_abstract_theoretical_rebuttals: Other-user comments: every comment relies solely on abstract theoretical rebuttals, with no specific verifiable procedural example.

argument_has_counter_question_marker: OP argument: 1 if the OP's own text contains at least one specific counter-question marker, i.e. a question posed to challenge or probe an opposing position or invite a counter-case; else 0.
op_argument_has_personal_anecdote: OP argument: 1 if it includes a personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative by the OP about their own experience.

any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_divergence: Other-user comments: at least one comment explicitly acknowledges the validity of the OP's premise (initial premise) and then introduces divergence/disagreement within the same comment.
any_comment_concrete_personal_anecdote: OC_comments (other users): 1 if at least one comment employs a concrete personal anecdote (the commenter's own specific experience) as part of its argument.

any_comment_abstract_reasoning: OC_comments (other users): 1 if at least one comment employs abstract reasoning (general principles, logic or conceptual argument rather than a concrete personal anecdote).

has_at_least_three_oc_comments: OC_comments: 1 if the list contains three or more comments, else 0

any_comment_direct_counterargument: Other-user comments (OC_comments, with OP title/argument as target context): 1 if at least one comment directly counterargues the OP's stated view, i.e. argues explicitly against it or a specific OP claim.

any_comment_redrafts_op_view_before_refuting: Other-user comments: at least one comment restates/rewrites the OP's viewpoint in a more nuanced form and then refutes that restated view, within the same comment.
post_score_above_50: Supplied observed original-post score: 1 if post_score > 50, else 0.
op_argument_explicit_uncertainty: OP argument: 1 if the OP's own text contains at least one explicit uncertainty marker (e.g., hedge or stated doubt about their own claims); else 0.
op_argument_acknowledges_counterargument_or_limitation: OP argument: 1 if the OP explicitly acknowledges a counter-argument to, or a limitation of, their own view; else 0.

any_comment_named_real_world_analogy: Other-user counter-argument comments: 1 if at least one comment uses a named, real-world analogy or case (e.g., specific historical or scientific example) to make its point.

any_comment_abstract_logical_rebuttal: Other-user counter-argument comments: 1 if at least one comment is an abstract logical rebuttal that relies on general reasoning without named real-world examples.

any_comment_contrasts_op_view_with_relatable_personal_experience: Other-user OC_comments: 1 if at least one comment explicitly contrasts the OP's view with a relatable real-world personal experience (the commenter's own or someone they personally know).

title_has_emotional_or_personal_identifier: OP title: 1 if the title contains an explicit emotional or personal identifier (e.g., stated feeling/emotion word, or first-person/self-identifying marker of the OP's own identity or experience).

any_comment_second_person_address_to_op: OC_comments: 1 if at least one other-user comment uses second-person direct address to the original poster (OP); else 0.

argument_has_first_person_singular_pronoun: OP argument: 1 if the OP's own argument text contains at least one explicit first-person singular pronoun (I, me, my, mine, myself, and contractions such as I'm/I've/I'd/I'll) used by the OP, excluding outcome-reporting text.
any_comment_presents_counterargument: Other-user OC_comments: 1 if at least one comment presents a counterargument to the OP's stated view (title/argument); else 0.
counterargument_cognitive_complexity: OC_comments (other users' counter-argument comments): overall cognitive complexity of the counterarguments, 0-10 anchored score

any_comment_acknowledges_op_valid_point_before_discrepancy: Other-user comments: 1 if at least one comment, within the same comment, explicitly acknowledges a valid point underlying the OP's view and only afterward introduces a discrepancy/disagreement with it.

any_comment_uses_analogy_to_familiar_scenario: OC_comments (other users' counter-argument comments): 1 if at least one comment uses an analogy to a familiar scenario as part of its argument

full_description: argument_compares_to_scientific_or_historical_norms: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, makes an explicit comparison between their claim, case or proposal and an established scientific norm (e.g. accepted scientific standard, consensus, or established finding/practice) or an established historical norm (e.g. a long-standing historical standard, practice or precedent), stating similarity or difference to it. Return 0 if the argument contains no such explicit comparison (mere mention of science or history without comparing to a norm does not count). Exclude quotations or positions attributed to others unless the OP adopts them. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they would otherwise qualify; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is not itself a scientific/historical norm comparison. Output a single 0/1 value. Return null if argument is missing or malformed. (dtype: binary)

op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation: Read the OP's title and argument (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly expresses fear or worry of social rejection or isolation (being rejected, ostracized, shunned, excluded or left alone by other people) connected to their view or its expression. Return 0 if no such explicit fear is present. Exclude quoted or reported other people's statements unless the OP adopts them as their own fear. Do not use any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; ignore such text entirely, but generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant. Do not reconstruct an initial version by removing edits. If title and argument are both missing or empty/malformed, return null. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense: Read the OP's title and argument (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP states their beliefs and reasons without any emotional self-defense, i.e. no expressions of fear, anxiety, hurt, defensiveness, or self-protective emotional appeals about themselves or their standing with others. Return 0 if any such emotional self-defense is present in the OP's own voice (including fear of social rejection or isolation). Exclude quoted or reported other people's statements unless the OP adopts them. Do not use any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; ignore such text entirely, but generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant. Do not reconstruct an initial version by removing edits. If title and argument are both missing or empty/malformed, return null. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

fear_rejection_vs_no_self_defense_group: Using `op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation` and `op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense` (both derived from title and argument): return 1 if df['op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation']==1; else return 0 if df['op_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense']==1; else null (rows with other emotional self-defense but no explicit fear of rejection/isolation, or missing inputs, are outside the two compared groups). (dtype: binary)

any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it; list order is not rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment cites a specific institutional precedent (a real, named or concretely identified institution, law, policy, program or system in a particular jurisdiction/organization) presented as actually functioning/operating in practice, used as support for that comment's counter-argument. Quoted material from others counts only if the commenter uses it as support. Purely abstract principles, hypothetical or invented systems, generic personal anecdotes without an institution, and non-functioning/failed precedents cited as support do not qualify. Ignore any text where the OP announces a view change or delta award, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies (including an empty list). Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output only 0, 1 or null. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it; list order is not rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment relies on abstract normative principles (general moral, ethical, rights-based, fairness or justice principles stated in general terms, about what ought to be) as the basis of its counter-argument. A comment that mainly rests on specific concrete cases, institutions or empirical facts does not qualify on that basis alone. Ignore any text where the OP announces a view change or delta award, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies (including an empty list). Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output only 0, 1 or null. (dtype: binary)

supplied_log_length: Return pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce') as the row value; null if missing or non-numeric. Use the supplied value unchanged (observed range about 0.69 to 7.44). Do not recompute it or convert it to a word count. (dtype: numeric)

op_argument_admits_uncertainty: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly admits uncertainty, doubt, or possibility of being wrong about their view or claims (e.g. 'I'm not sure', 'I could be wrong', 'I may be mistaken'). Return 0 if the argument is present and contains no such explicit admission. Ignore quoted others' text or opponents' positions unless the OP adopts it as their own. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even within the argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. Return null if the argument is missing or malformed. (dtype: binary)

op_argument_asserts_absolute_certainty: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their view (e.g. 'I am 100% certain', 'there is no possible way I'm wrong', 'undeniably true'), leaving no room for error. Ordinary confident phrasing without explicit absolute-certainty claims returns 0, as does an argument with no such assertion. Ignore quoted others' text or opponents' positions unless the OP adopts it. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even within the argument); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. Return null if the argument is missing or malformed. (dtype: binary)

distinct_op_factual_premises_challenged: Read the OP's argument and parse OC_comments (a JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP; list order is not chronology or rank). Identify the distinct factual premises (empirical/factual claims, not purely normative or value claims) asserted by the OP in the argument. Count how many distinct such premises are challenged (disputed, contradicted, or shown to be false/unsupported) by at least one comment; a premise challenged by several comments counts once, and one comment challenging several different premises counts each. Do not count challenges to value judgments, conclusions that are purely normative, or the OP's wording only. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither an announcement nor a premise to count. Use current supplied text including marked edits; do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. Output a non-negative integer: 0 = comments challenge no OP factual premise; 1 = one; 2 = two; etc. If OC_comments is a valid empty list, output 0. If argument or OC_comments is missing or malformed, output null. (dtype: numeric)

oc_comment_count: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list; return len(list) (non-negative integer). Valid empty list -> 0. Missing or malformed/unparseable value -> null. Counts comments, not distinct commenters or arguments; order is ignored. (dtype: numeric)

distinct_counterargument_count: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP), with title and argument only as context to identify the OP's view. Count the distinct counter-arguments the comments make against the OP's view; a counter-argument is a separate reason, objection, or piece of evidence challenging the OP's position. Deduplicate semantically: the same argument repeated in several comments, or restated within one comment, counts once; one comment can contribute several distinct arguments. Do not count agreement with the OP, clarifying questions, jokes, or moderator/bot notices. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (even in argument or comments); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is not itself a counter-argument unless it challenges the OP's view. Output a non-negative integer. A valid empty comment list gives 0. If OC_comments is missing or malformed, output null. Use current supplied text; no chronology is implied by list order. (dtype: numeric)

has_at_least_three_distinct_counterarguments: Using `distinct_counterargument_count`: return null if df['distinct_counterargument_count'] is null; return 1 if df['distinct_counterargument_count'] >= 3, else 0. (dtype: binary)

title_uses_absolute_certainty_markers: Read only the title column (the OP's heading). Return 1 if the title itself uses absolute certainty markers, i.e. wording that presents the claim as completely certain, exceptionless or beyond doubt (e.g. universal/absolute quantifiers or certainty expressions such as 'all', 'always', 'never', 'no one', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'definitely'); these are examples, not an exhaustive list or extra requirements. Return 0 if the title has no such markers, including when it is hedged or tentative (e.g. 'generally', 'I think'). Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Ignore any text reporting a view change, delta award, thank-you or resolution update, or the outcome (none expected in titles); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not such an announcement. If the title is missing or empty, return null. Output a single value: 1, 0, or null. (dtype: binary)

op_invites_critique_or_tentative: Read the OP's title and argument (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if, in the OP's own voice, the OP explicitly invites critique, counter-arguments or challenge to their view (e.g. asking to be convinced or shown wrong) OR expresses their view with tentative/hedged language (e.g. 'I think', 'maybe', 'I might be wrong', 'not sure', 'it seems'). Return 0 if neither is present. Exclude quotations of other people or reported opponents' positions unless the OP adopts them as their own. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant. Do not treat the generic subreddit framing alone as an explicit invitation unless the OP's own text says so. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot; use supplied current text. If both title and argument are missing or malformed return null. Output a single 0/1 or null. (dtype: binary)

op_uses_absolute_definitive_declarations: Read the OP's title and argument (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if, in the OP's own voice, the OP states their view in absolute or definitive declarations (e.g. categorical claims such as 'always', 'never', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'there is no way', unqualified certainty stated as fact). Return 0 if no such absolute/definitive declaration is present. Absence of tentative language alone does not make a text absolute; require affirmative absolute/definitive wording. Exclude quotations of other people or reported opponents' positions unless the OP adopts them as their own. Exclude any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; do not use them as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot; use supplied current text. If both title and argument are missing or malformed return null. Output a single 0/1 or null. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example: Read OC_comments, a JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example, i.e. a concrete actual case, event, person, organization, place, study instance, or specific personal experience offered to support or illustrate its argument. The example need not be externally verified, and any domain qualifies. Invented, hypothetical, or purely generic scenarios and abstract generalizations do not count. Ignore any text reporting OP view change, delta awards, post-outcome thanks/resolution updates or whether the outcome occurred; such text is not evidence (generic discussion of delta/platform rules is allowed but is not an example by itself). Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 or null. (dtype: binary)

share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. If missing/malformed return null; if a valid empty list return null (share undefined). For each comment decide whether it contains measured, logical reasoning: calm, structured argumentation that draws inferences from premises or evidence to a conclusion in a restrained tone. A comment may contain both this and emotional aggression; it counts here if it contains measured logical reasoning. Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible. Output a number in [0,1]: the number of comments with measured logical reasoning divided by the total number of comments. 0 means none do. Comment order is irrelevant. (dtype: numeric)

share_comments_emotional_aggression: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. If missing/malformed return null; if a valid empty list return null (share undefined). For each comment decide whether it contains emotional aggression: hostile, angry, insulting, contemptuous or belligerent emotional language directed at the OP or others. Mere disagreement, firm or critical tone, or generic emotional wording without hostility does not count. Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. A comment may contain both aggression and logical reasoning; it counts here if it contains aggression. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules remains eligible. Output a number in [0,1]: comments with emotional aggression divided by total comments. 0 means none do. (dtype: numeric)

logical_minus_aggressive_comment_share: Using `share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning` and `share_comments_emotional_aggression`: return df['share_comments_measured_logical_reasoning'] - df['share_comments_emotional_aggression']; null if either is null. (dtype: numeric)

any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim: Read title, argument (OP text; use as context to identify OP factual claims) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP). Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly quotes (directly, or a close verbatim excerpt matching OP title/argument text) a specific factual claim made by the OP and (b) argues that this same factual claim is false or wrong. Quote and refutation must be in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Merely mentioning the OP's topic, quoting a non-factual opinion/value claim, or quoting without refuting gives no match. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, in the argument or comments; do not use them as evidence (generic discussion of delta/platform rules is allowed where relevant). Use current supplied text including marked edits; no initial snapshot is assumed. Return 0 if OC_comments is a valid empty list or no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if title and argument are both missing so that a quote match cannot be assessed (a positive match observed against available OP text still gives 1). (dtype: binary)

any_comment_validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly validates the OP personally (their dignity, worth, or effort, e.g. praising their effort or thoughtfulness, or affirming them as a person) and, afterwards within that same comment, introduces corrective logic (reasoning meant to correct or counter the OP's view). The validation must be directed at the OP as a person or their effort, not merely agreement with or praise of a claim; validation and correction must co-occur in the same comment with validation coming first. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Ignore quoted text from others unless adopted by the commenter. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Use only current supplied text; no timing is inferred. (dtype: binary)

all_comments_purely_logical_refutation: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if every comment is a logical/argumentative refutation of the OP's view and none contains explicit validation of the OP's personal dignity or effort (praise or affirmation of the OP as a person or their effort). Return 0 if the list is non-empty and at least one comment contains such validation or is not a logical refutation. Return null for a valid empty list, or if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Exclude any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Use only current supplied text; no timing is inferred. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_concrete_real_world_example: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment itself provides a concrete real-world example in support of its argument: a specific actual case, event, person, institution, data instance or concrete personal experience that really occurred. Purely abstract principles/reasoning, generic claims, and invented or hypothetical scenarios do not count; named examples need not be externally verified, and the example need not belong to any particular type (institutional, public or personal all qualify). Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty but no comment contains one. Return 0 for a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. List order carries no meaning. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if they appear in comments; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered if relevant. Output a single 0/1 or null. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_engages_op_cited_examples_or_premises: Read title, argument (OP's text) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly engages with a specific example or premise actually stated in the OP's title or argument (e.g. names, quotes, paraphrases and then addresses, rebuts, or builds on that particular example or premise). Generic replies that only address the overall topic or the conclusion without referring to a specific OP example/premise return 0 for that comment. Agreement or disagreement both count if explicit engagement is present; endorsement is not required. Use OP text only to identify targets. Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in the argument; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement. Use supplied current text (including marked edits) apart from that exclusion; no chronology is inferred from list order. Return 0 if OC_comments is a valid empty list; return null if OC_comments or the OP text is missing or malformed. Output one scalar 0/1. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_concrete_personal_labor_details: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment introduces concrete, personal labor-process details: specific, particular descriptions of how work is actually done (tasks, workplace procedures, working conditions, job experiences) drawn from the commenter's own or a specifically described person's experience. Abstract generalities about work, hypothetical or invented scenarios, and purely normative principles do not qualify. Quoted text from others counts only if the commenter adopts it as their own experience. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution text and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither positive evidence nor an outcome announcement. Use current supplied text; list order carries no meaning. Return 0 if the list is valid and empty or no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

all_comments_solely_abstract_normative: Read OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if every comment relies solely on abstract normative principles (general claims about what is right, fair, just or ought to be) with no concrete factual examples or personal experiences. Return 0 if the list is non-empty and at least one comment contains any concrete, personal, or empirical-example content. Return null if the list is empty or OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution text and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and is judged like other content. Use current supplied text; list order carries no meaning. Output a single 0/1 value or null. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_quantifies_systemic_material_harm_to_third_parties: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quantifies systemic (institutional, structural or society-wide, not merely isolated) material harm (e.g., deaths, money, jobs, health, housing, resources lost) to third parties, i.e. people other than the commenter, by giving numbers, rates, amounts, proportions or explicit magnitudes. Vague harm claims without any quantity, purely abstract/moral/propositional arguments, and harms only to the commenter or hypothetical individuals do not count. Quoted material counts only if the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither positive evidence nor to be treated as outcome reporting. Use current supplied text; list order carries no meaning. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies (including empty list). Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 per row. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_asserts_propositional_falsity: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; parse it) and the OP title and argument as context for identifying the OP's claims. Return 1 if at least one comment asserts that a proposition or claim made by the OP (in title or argument) is false, incorrect or logically unsound, i.e. disputes its truth rather than describing consequences. Quoted material counts only if the commenter adopts it. Comments that only add harms, offer opinions, or agree do not count. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, in any field; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not outcome reporting. Use current supplied text; list order carries no meaning. Return 0 if the comment list is valid (including empty) and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/malformed, or if OP title and argument are both missing. Output a single 0/1 per row. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_identifies_op_internal_contradiction: Read title, argument and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP). Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one comment argues that the OP's own stated premises (as written in title/argument) contradict each other or are mutually inconsistent, i.e. a logical contradiction internal to the OP's position. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does so (including comments that only dispute premises using outside facts, or only disagree). Return 0 for a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing/malformed or if title and argument are both missing. Use current supplied text, including marked edits. Ignore and never use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, wherever they appear; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. List order carries no meaning. The same comment may also cite external evidence; this does not affect the value. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_cites_external_evidence: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users, not the OP). Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one comment cites evidence external to the OP's post in support of its counter-argument, such as statistics, studies, named sources, links, or specific documented real-world facts or cases. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does so (including purely logical/internal-consistency arguments, opinion, or hypotheticals). Return 0 for a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore and never use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred, wherever they appear; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. List order carries no meaning. The same comment may also identify a contradiction; this does not affect the value. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_specific_factual_data_or_citation: Read OC_comments, a JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP. Return 1 if at least one comment itself offers specific factual data (e.g. concrete statistics, figures, dates, named studies, documented facts or events) or a verifiable citation/reference (e.g. a link, named source, author, publication, law or case) in support of its argument. Vague assertions, general opinion, reasoning without specific data, and purely hypothetical scenarios do not count. A source quoted only as an opponent's position and not offered as support by the commenter does not count. Ignore any text that is an OP view-change or delta-award announcement, a post-outcome thank-you/resolution update, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither such an announcement nor evidence of data. Judge the supplied current text; order of comments is not meaningful. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including a valid empty list; return null if the list is missing or malformed. (dtype: binary)

argument_has_polite_apology_phrase: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP's own wording contains at least one explicit polite apology phrase (e.g., 'sorry', 'I apologize', 'apologies for', 'my apologies', 'pardon me', 'excuse my'), whether apologizing for length, formatting, wording, or anything else. Return 0 if the argument is present and has no such phrase. Do not count apologies inside quotations attributed to other speakers or quoted material not adopted by the OP, and do not count 'sorry' used non-apologetically (e.g., 'sorry state of affairs'). Ignore and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, or text reporting whether the outcome occurred (including apologies or thanks within such passages); generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Do not reconstruct an initial snapshot. If the argument is missing or malformed, return null. Output a single 0/1 or null. (dtype: binary)

op_first_person_vulnerable_admission: Read the OP's title and argument (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, speaking in their own first-person voice, makes at least one vulnerable admission: a disclosure of their own personal weakness, fear, failure, insecurity, mistake, struggle or emotionally exposing experience. Return 0 if the text is assessable and contains no such admission (merely stating opinions, or first-person statements that are not self-exposing, do not count). Ignore quoted or reported words of other people unless the OP explicitly adopts them as their own admission. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the view changed; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither evidence nor an outcome announcement. Do not try to reconstruct an initial version. Return null if title and argument are both missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

op_third_person_distant_observation: Read the OP's title and argument (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP presents at least one distant third-person observation: a detached description or observation about other people, groups, institutions, society or events, made from an external standpoint without personal involvement or self-disclosure. Return 0 if the text is assessable and contains no such observation. Ignore quotations of other users unless the OP adopts them as their own observation. Exclude and do not use as evidence any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the view changed; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is neither evidence nor an outcome announcement. Do not try to reconstruct an initial version. Return null if title and argument are both missing or malformed. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

vulnerable_admission_vs_distant_observation_only: Using `op_first_person_vulnerable_admission` and `op_third_person_distant_observation`: return null if either is null; return 1 if df['op_first_person_vulnerable_admission']==1 and df['op_third_person_distant_observation']==0; return 0 if df['op_first_person_vulnerable_admission']==0 and df['op_third_person_distant_observation']==1; otherwise (both 1 or both 0) return null. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_contains_url: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings. If missing or malformed, return null. If the list is valid but empty, return 0. Otherwise return 1 if any comment matches the case-insensitive regex r'(https?://|www\.)\S+' or contains a markdown link of the form [text](http...), else 0. Pandas sketch: lst=json.loads(x); int(any(re.search(r'(https?://|www\.)\S+', c, re.I) for c in lst)). Literal matching only; it does not check whether the link works or supports the argument. Only OC_comments is read, so OP outcome announcements in argument or conversation are not used. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_specific_verifiable_procedural_example: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP); parse it. Return 1 if at least one comment employs, in its own counter-argument, a specific example of a procedure or process (e.g. how a legal, institutional, administrative, technical or scientific procedure actually works or was applied) that is concrete and checkable in principle (specific enough to be verified; no outside verification is actually needed). Quoted material counts only if the commenter uses it as support. Purely abstract, theoretical, hypothetical or invented scenarios do not count; generic assertions without a specific procedure do not count. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

all_comments_solely_abstract_theoretical_rebuttals: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP); parse it. Return 1 if the list is non-empty and every comment's counter-argument relies solely on abstract or theoretical reasoning, with no specific, verifiable procedural example (concrete checkable process, procedure, rule application or documented case) in any comment. Return 0 if at least one comment contains such a specific verifiable procedural example or other concrete case-based support. Return null if OC_comments is empty, missing or malformed. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates and text reporting whether the outcome occurred; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

argument_has_counter_question_marker: Read only the OP's argument text (not title, comments or conversation). Return 1 if the OP's own wording contains at least one specific counter-question marker: an explicit question (usually ending in '?' or phrased interrogatively) that the OP poses to counter, challenge or probe an opposing position, or to ask readers for a counter-argument, counterexample or rebuttal on a particular point (e.g. 'what about X?', 'how would you explain Y?', 'can anyone show a case where...?'). Return 0 if the argument has no such question; questions that are purely rhetorical scene-setting with no challenge/probe/counter-invitation, and questions inside external quotations or reported text from others not adopted by the OP, do not count. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred (including edits such as 'EDIT: my view was changed'); these never count as evidence. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and remains eligible. Use the supplied current text, including marked edits, subject to that exclusion. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; an assessable argument with no marker gives 0. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

op_argument_has_personal_anecdote: Read only the OP's argument text (current supplied text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP's own text includes a personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative, i.e. the OP recounts a specific experience, event or situation they personally lived through or participated in (e.g. 'when I worked at...', 'my friend and I...'). Return 0 if the argument is assessable and contains none: purely abstract claims, hypotheticals/invented scenarios, general statements, or experiences only of others/quoted external sources not adopted as the OP's own. Do not count mere first-person opinion phrases ('I think') as narrative. Exclude and ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you/resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the view changed, even if they contain first-person narrative; generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be considered where relevant. Do not attempt to reconstruct an initial version of the post. If the argument is missing or malformed, return null. Output a single 0/1 value. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_divergence: Read title, argument (OP's view) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment, within that same comment, first explicitly acknowledges that the OP's initial premise (a starting premise/claim of the OP's view, identified from title and argument) is valid, correct or reasonable (e.g. concedes a point as right), and afterwards introduces a point of divergence, disagreement or counter-argument. Both parts must be in the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Vague politeness, mere topical engagement, or acknowledging only that the OP has feelings or tried, without conceding validity of the premise, does not count. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, including an empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if title and argument are both missing so that the OP premise cannot be identified. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome thank-you or resolution updates, and any text reporting whether the outcome occurred, even if in the argument; do not use them as evidence of the OP premise or anything else. Generic discussion of delta/platform rules is not an outcome announcement and may be retained. Use current supplied text; no initial snapshot is inferred, and list order is not chronology. (dtype: binary)

any_comment_concrete_personal_anecdote: Read OC_comments, a JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP. Parse the list. Return 1 if at least one comment employs a concrete personal anecdote, i.e. the commenter recounts a specific experience of their own (or first-hand event involving themselves) as part of their argument. Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty and no comment does so (generic reasoning, hypotheticals, others' stories, external quotations, and statistics are not personal anecdotes).
